findings.evidence: all bear on the root's composition; train split for data-level numbers

findings.statement: domain reading
findings.evidence: age, smoking, obesity (bmi ~30) and low income raise predicted risk; insurance, female sex, urban living and a higher score lower it slightly; nothing conflicts with general knowledge. The noise input's effect (larger than five real inputs at the typical case) is flagged by the record itself as a fitted weight

bmi_obesity_hinge.why: An obesity threshold: the unit is off below a bmi of about 29-30 (28.4 to 31.1 depending on the other inputs) and rises steeply above it, taking the typical case from 11% to 86% by bmi 36, with age and income moving it little.

nonsmoker_young_affluent_unit.why: Smoking does switch it off for most smokers (2157 of 7255 keep it) and it lowers risk for younger, richer, leaner non-smokers, but it reads the noise input about as strongly as income and moves the training AUC only from 0.913 to 0.911.

low_income_hinge.why: A poverty threshold near 50 thousand at age 50 whose cut-off moves up with age (about 45 at 35, about 55 at 70) and adds up to 3 logit units at income 10; only income's effect above the threshold is left to other units and is understated as 'a little'.

age_smoker_ramp.why: Carries the main age effect (risk rises steadily with age on the logit scale, shifted up by smoking and lower income) and switches off for the oldest, earlier for smokers; on the data it is almost linear (R2 0.989), so the switch-off is a saturation detail on 1056 rows, as the hypothesis itself says.
